classification.difficultyReason: Apply the preceding feature-analysis procedure independently to four translated and reflected parabolas.

content.prompt: Repeat the steps of Question 1 in order to sketch the graphs of these quadratic functions: identify the concavity; substitute $x=0$ for the $y$-intercept; find the axis and vertex from completed-square form; explain why there are $x$-intercepts and calculate them by putting $y=0$; then sketch each graph showing all key features.

answer.worked:
The coefficient of the square is positive, so the parabola is concave up. Its axis is $x=-1$ and vertex is $(-1,-4)$.
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=(0+1)^2-4\\y(0)&=-3\end{align*}$$
The vertex is below the $x$-axis and the parabola opens upwards, so it crosses twice.
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x+1)^2-4\\(x+1)^2&=4\\x+1&=\pm2\\x&=-3\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
Sketch a smooth upward-opening curve through these intercepts and the vertex, symmetric about $x=-1$.

spec.description: Complete answer graph with dashed symmetry axis.

answer.worked:
The coefficient of the square is positive, so the parabola is concave up. Its axis is $x=1$ and vertex is $(1,-9)$.
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=(0-1)^2-9\\y(0)&=-8\end{align*}$$
The upward-opening parabola has its vertex below the $x$-axis, so it crosses twice.
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x-1)^2-9\\(x-1)^2&=9\\x-1&=\pm3\\x&=-2\text{ or }4\end{align*}$$
Draw a smooth curve through the vertex and intercepts, symmetric about $x=1$.

spec.description: Complete answer graph with dashed symmetry axis.

answer.worked:
The coefficient of the square is negative, so the parabola is concave down. Its axis is $x=-2$ and vertex is $(-2,4)$.
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=-(0+2)^2+4\\y(0)&=0\end{align*}$$
The downward-opening parabola has its vertex above the $x$-axis, so it crosses twice.
$$\begin{align*}0&=-(x+2)^2+4\\(x+2)^2&=4\\x+2&=\pm2\\x&=-4\text{ or }0\end{align*}$$
Draw a smooth downward-opening curve through the vertex and intercepts, symmetric about $x=-2$.

spec.description: Authored solution graph, including the intercept at the origin as a coordinate label.
